summary: The exact candidate passes the full 93-test mutation suite, full 15-test decision suite, manifest freshness, prelock validator, source extraction, 1,098-file source-staging check, project-status validator, and diff check after the explicitly permitted ignored sources are staged. The corrected inventory helper currently derives the complete independently recomputed set of 57 forbidden paths and 30 forbidden identifiers, and the test exercises every returned member as an exact key and an embedded value. Candidate 5 is not green: all 30 identifiers still bypass source-only validation when embedded in a decorated JSON member name; three inventory-omission mutants survive the purported exhaustive control because it iterates the implementation's own returned sets; and PROJECT_STATUS.md retains a contradictory dirty/pending-candidate-5 statement at a clean committed candidate-5 HEAD.

findings.title: Decorated JSON member names still leak every forbidden post-reveal identifier
findings.contract: The source-only preflight must reject every forbidden inventory member before canonical completeness or blind prompt bytes are emitted, whether the identifier occurs in a JSON string value or a JSON object member name.
findings.claim: scripts/build_correctness_audit_prompt.py compares a member name to forbidden_identifiers by exact equality, while it scans string values with identifier-boundary regular expressions. A member name such as 'meta:rootCauseId!' or 'fixture authorityOverride fixture' therefore passes even though the identical text as a value is rejected. JSON member names are serialized into the source-only prompt, and the builder does not schema-validate packet or completeness payloads before framing them.

evidence.detail: The dict branch uses `key in forbidden_identifiers`; the string branch uses boundary-aware regex matching. Path keys use substring matching, so the residual asymmetry is identifier-specific.
Both canonical prompt modes call the same source-only payload validator before framing, with no schema validation that would remove arbitrary member names.

The corrected matrix uses each identifier only as an exact key (`{identifier: 'fixture'}`), while its value case decorates the identifier inside a longer string. It never applies the value boundary cases to member-name text.

evidence.result: For all 30 derived identifiers, exact keys were rejected 30/30 and the same decorated text as a value was rejected 30/30, but space-decorated keys were rejected 0/30 and punctuation-decorated keys were rejected 0/30.

evidence.detail: The retained blocker requires rejection regardless of whether a token occurs as a value or object member name and notes that schema-invalid payloads can be emitted because the prompt builder does not perform schema validation.

findings.impact: A source packet or accepted completeness payload can place rootCauseId, authorityOverride, verificationEvidenceRefs, or any other forbidden identifier inside a syntactically valid JSON member name and have that post-reveal vocabulary emitted to completeness or blind reviewers. This leaves the candidate-4 blindness defect only partially fixed despite the green suite.
findings.recommendation: Apply the same boundary-aware identifier scan to every string member name before descending, while retaining the explicit source/completeness/shared allowlists. Add exact, space-delimited, and punctuation-delimited key cases for every derived identifier through both canonical prompt modes and verify no output creation or sentinel overwrite on rejection.

findings.title: The exhaustive inventory control is self-referential and does not kill inventory-derivation omissions
findings.contract: A mutation control claiming exhaustive coverage of all manifest/schema-derived forbidden members must independently assert the expected derived universe, not merely iterate whatever universe the implementation under test returns.
findings.claim: test_source_only_inventory_covers_frozen_paths_and_post_reveal_ids obtains both sets directly from source_only_forbidden_inventory(), asserts only one path and six identifiers, and then loops those same sets. Removing an otherwise required path or identifier from the production inventory shrinks the test loop and remains green. The control also does not implement the retained candidate-4 request for a per-member completeness/blind CLI matrix with absent and pre-existing sentinel outputs.

evidence.detail: Only scripts/build_semantic_pilots.py and six named identifiers are independently pinned; every other member is trusted from the function under test.

evidence.result: The focused control passed when docs/rules/ontology/mappings.json was removed, passed when sourceFinding was removed, and passed when the entire inventory was collapsed to the one asserted path plus six asserted identifiers: 3/3 omission mutants survived.

Independent current-state recomputation nevertheless confirms the unmutated implementation now returns the correct 57 paths and 30 identifiers with no missing or unexpected members; the finding is about claimed mutation coverage and future drift detection, not a current raw inventory omission.

evidence.detail: The retained minimal fix calls for every identifier as a key, every path/identifier as a string through completeness and blind canonical CLI modes, and absent/sentinel output preservation. Candidate 5 exercises only the helper and exact-key shape.

findings.impact: The 93/93 result is a false green for the stated exhaustive derivation property. A future or deliberate omission in a manifest section, unit target field, fixed set, comparison schema, or audit-result schema can survive this control, and the candidate-5 status/disposition cannot rely on the test to prove inventory completeness.
findings.recommendation: Independently derive the expected sets in the test from the manifest sections, unit fields, closed schemas, and explicit allowlists; assert exact set equality and stable headline counts. Add omission mutants for every derivation source and the retained per-member completeness/blind prewrite matrix.
